newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bomb threat empties Mexico City office building.
newsitem.headline: Bomb threat empties Mexico City office building.

text.p: A telephoned bomb threat forced the evacuation of a 20-floor office building across the street from the U.S. Embassy on Tuesday, but the threat was a false alarm, witnesses said.

The threat interrupted mid-day work routines for about 10 companies including American Airlines and the giant Mexican tortilla and corn-flour company Grupo Maseca. The U.S. Embassy was unaffected and workers there were unaware of the incident, a spokeswoman said.

Security guards at the building on the capital's main Reforma avenue said office workers were cleared to return to work after waiting outside for about an hour. But some employees said they would take the afternoon off after being told they could return at their own risk.

"Some guy called saying that he didn't want to hurt anybody but that there was a bomb," one office worker told Reuters, asking not to reveal her name or the name of her company. "He called back about five minutes later saying the bomb would explode in 15 minutes but nothing happened."
The woman said she was a co-worker of the woman who received the call.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the hoax. Since the appearance at in June of a new Marxist guerrilla group, the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), there have been occasional bomb threats in some Mexican cities but the EPR has denied responsibility for them.
